body: [{"streamId":"01a0c941-fb35-74fe-9102-978de06852f4","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Decision.DecisionRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a0c941-fb35-74fe-9102-978de06852f4\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022**The five \\u0060ProcessManagerParityTests\\u0060 failures on windows-latest across PR #311 (job 102959750110, run 34503487599 attempt 1, 2026-09-10 12:43 EDT), PR #312 (job 102994544797, run 34513922486 attempt 1, 2026-09-10 14:26 EDT) and PR #313 (job 103114197866, run 34551170786 attempt 1, 2026-09-10 21:39 EDT) trace to this repo\\u0027s own concurrently-scheduled test classes starving the runner, not to a race in \\u0060TerminateTree\\u0060 or its grace window; the fix serializes \\u0060ProcessManagerParityTests\\u0060 against the suite\\u0027s other real-process-spawning classes in a shared collection rather than widening any deadline or retuning a daemon constant.** Why: none of the three pull requests touches \\u0060src/Hall9k.Daemon/ProcessManagement\\u0060, and main\\u0027s own windows-latest legs (at least twelve runs through a2c91e6d) pass, so the failures were diagnosed against the runner rather than assumed racy, per this task\\u0027s own instruction. Reading the three jobs\\u0027 raw logs (\\u0060gh api repos/Hallmanac/hall9k/actions/jobs/\\u003Cid\\u003E/logs\\u0060) by their own xUnit elapsed-time stamps names the actual cause, and which class overlapped which failure is not the same fixed pair across all three: PR #311\\u0027s own 20s failure window (job 102959750110, roughly 12:43:24 to 12:43:44 EDT) was filled for its entire span not by \\u0060GitWorktreeManagerTests\\u0060 or \\u0060RepoMaterialiserTests\\u0060, whose first results that run logged at 12:43:46 and 12:43:52 EDT respectively (the latter eight seconds after the failure was already logged, the former overlapping only the window\\u0027s last four seconds), but by \\u0060Hall9k.Tests.Daemon.Review.DecisionsLogRenumbererTransitionTests\\u0060 and \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumbererFixtureTests\\u0060, two classes that shell out to real \\u0060git\\u0060 many times per test through \\u0060RunRebasedOntoBase\\u0060 and carried no \\u0060[Collection]\\u0060 of their own, running continuously across the whole window (Transition\\u0027s own tests finished at 12:43:22, :26, :26, :29, :42 and :43.9 EDT, the last one closing barely a tenth of a second before the failure was logged at 12:43:44.0; Fixture\\u0027s own 15s test finished at 12:43:26 EDT). PR #312\\u0027s and #313\\u0027s own windows are the pairing the earlier version of this entry described: \\u0060GitWorktreeManagerTests\\u0060 and \\u0060RepoMaterialiserTests\\u0060 were both mid-test at the exact moment each of those failures was logged, each of those two classes\\u0027 own individual tests running 2-43 seconds under that windows-latest contention against the same PR\\u0027s own ubuntu-latest leg, where the identical tests each finish in well under a second (job 102959749710\\u0027s own log, PR #311) with nothing else fighting them for the runner; \\u0060Hall9k.Tests.Domain.CrossProcessContainerGateTests\\u0060\\u0027 own real \\u0060dotnet\\u0060 child also overlapped PR #312\\u0027s window. \\u0060Hall9k.Tests.Daemon.TestScopeResolverTests\\u0060, another real-\\u0060git\\u0060 spawner, was concurrently running in two of the three (#311, #312). Two failure shapes, one cause, and, checked against each job\\u0027s own error text rather than trusted from this task\\u0027s own inherited paraphrase, the split is not the one-PR-per-shape pairing it looks like at a glance: four of the five failures are the same setup-deadline shape, \\u0060#311\\u0060\\u0027s own included (job 102959750110\\u0027s actual error is \\u0060AwaitNestedChildAsync\\u0060\\u0027s \\u0060The nested child\\u0027s pid file never appeared\\u0060, not a teardown assertion), plus all three of \\u0060#313\\u0060\\u0027s, where contention slowed the nested \\u0060cmd.exe\\u0060/\\u0060powershell.exe\\u0060/\\u0060ping.exe\\u0060 spawn chain itself past the shared 20s \\u0060ObservationDeadline\\u0060 before there was anything to assert on at all. Only \\u0060#312\\u0060\\u0027s single failure is the teardown-assertion shape: the spawn succeeded, but the WMI \\u0060Get-CimInstance Win32_Process\\u0060 query \\u0060WindowsProcessManager.CollectDescendants\\u0060 shells out to (or the native process kill/reap itself) was slow enough under the same contention that \\u0060TerminateTree\\u0060\\u0027s 500ms \\u0060LingeringGraceWindow\\u0060 and the test\\u0027s own 20s \\u0060ObservationDeadline\\u0060 poll both ran out before the reparented descendant was found and killed (the job log\\u0027s own \\u0022[29 s]\\u0022 against that test is its total elapsed run time including setup, not a distinct poll bound). \\u0060CollectDescendants\\u0060 is documented best-effort and silently returns empty on its own 5s \\u0060ChildProcessQueryTimeout\\u0060, so a starved WMI query can make a genuinely-alive descendant look un-findable rather than merely slow to find. Widening \\u0060ObservationDeadline\\u0060 or \\u0060ChildProcessQueryTimeout\\u0060 would not be honest here (this task\\u0027s own boundary): the runner was not merely slow, it was contended by this repo\\u0027s own concurrently-scheduled \\u0060git\\u0060/\\u0060dotnet\\u0060-spawning tests, so a wider bound only hides the same contention behind a longer wait rather than removing it, and does nothing for a run where the contention is worse still. Serializing the classes against each other is the same idea Decisions Log #158 already established for \\u0060PublishesBinary\\u0060 (no two real \\u0060dotnet publish\\u0060 callers run at once because they share \\u0060obj/Release\\u0060): here the shared resource is the runner\\u0027s own process-creation throughput rather than a directory. It is not the same mechanism, though: \\u0060PublishesBinary\\u0060 membership is guarded mechanically, \\u0060PublishLaneGuardTests\\u0060 fails the build if a third publish test is added without it, because every caller goes through one named helper, \\u0060PublishTestSupport.RunPublishAsync\\u0060. There is no equivalent single call site for \\u0022spawns real processes heavily enough to contend\\u0022 (\\u0060GitDescribedVersionTests\\u0060 spawns \\u0060git\\u0060 exactly once and stays out, \\u0060GitWorktreeManagerTests\\u0060 spawns it dozens of times per test and joins), so membership in \\u0060RealProcessSpawn\\u0060 is a judgment call recorded here and in \\u0060tests/Hall9k.Tests/README.md\\u0060, not a mechanically-enforced one. A plain \\u0060[Collection(\\u0022RealProcessSpawn\\u0022)]\\u0060 string, no \\u0060CollectionDefinition\\u0060 or fixture needed, applies to \\u0060ProcessManagerParityTests\\u0060, \\u0060GitWorktreeManagerTests\\u0060, \\u0060RepoMaterialiserTests\\u0060, \\u0060TestScopeResolverTests\\u0060, \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumbererTransitionTests\\u0060, \\u0060DecisionsLogRenumbererFixtureTests\\u0060 and \\u0060CrossProcessContainerGateTests\\u0060, each carrying a doc comment pointing back to this entry. This task\\u0027s own acceptance criteria name a further candidate by hand: PR #313\\u0027s own branch also adds \\u0060Hall9k.Tests.Integration.VerificationRunnerTests\\u0060, gate-shell tests that spawn real shells and \\u0060git\\u0060 through \\u0060TestGit\\u0060. That class stays in \\u0060[Collection(\\u0022Hall9kHome\\u0022)]\\u0060 rather than joining \\u0060RealProcessSpawn\\u0060: xUnit allows one collection per class, \\u0060Hall9kHome\\u0060 already serializes it against roughly four dozen other classes for install-directory isolation reasons unrelated to this contention and outside this task\\u0027s own boundary to retune without evidence, its own \\u0060git\\u0060 usage is a handful of short seed commands per test rather than the dozens-per-test throughput pattern the classes above show, and it never overlapped any of the three failing windows checked here. windows-latest CI itself never schedules \\u0060VerificationRunnerTests\\u0060 next to \\u0060ProcessManagerParityTests\\u0060 at all (\\u0060ci.yml\\u0060 filters \\u0060Category=RequiresDocker\\u0060 off that leg), so the only place this residual risk can still occur is the Windows node\\u0027s own full, unfiltered suite; that gap is named here rather than left silent, and the same reasoning covers \\u0060Hall9kHome\\u0060\\u0027s other real-process-spawning classes (for example \\u0060RunSupervisorTests\\u0060). facts before the gate ever runs: \\u0060PreFinalPassRebaseAwaitingGate\\u0060 is still set (cleared the moment a full-scope gate actually passes over the rebased tip) and this purpose: its own trailing-no-op guard deliberately leaves it pointing at an earlier real rebase across a later, unrelated no-op re-check, which would wrongly read as \\u0022the last rebase was sharing \\u0060RebaseRecovery\\u0060\\u0027s, bounded by its own \\u0060MaxSettlingGateRepairRounds\\u0060 cap (default 1) rather than the rebase-recovery cap. session that exits at once with no work done \\u2014 one turn, zero tokens, sub-second \\u2014 is classified as the node failing to launch a working session, never as the task\\u0027s own failure: the daemon raises a node-wide launch hold instead of failing the run or spending its ordinary in-place retry, stops claiming new work while the hold stands, and clears it only once a relaunch it can trust as fresh evidence actually runs.** Why: the 2026-09-07 outage\\u0027s own sessions all shared one shape \\u2014 one turn, zero input and output tokens, 85 to 208 ms \\u2014 for two unrelated causes observed in the same window, an expired OAuth credential and a GitHub fetch timeout, and the next cause will be a third string; classifying on that numeric shape (\\u0060LaunchFailureClassifier\\u0060), never on message text, is what lets one hold cover every future cause instead of a text list chasing each one after the fact. Text still wins for the one case that could otherwise be mistaken for it: a usage-limit result can itself carry this exact shape, so \\u0060BudgetExhaustionParser\\u0060 is checked first and always wins the budget park, never the launch hold. The hold is node-wide and blocks \\u0060DispatchEngine\\u0060\\u0027s own claim gate, not per-task, because the true fault is the node\\u0027s own ability to launch anything, and failing each queued task one by one behind an unreachable API would only spend every task\\u0027s own one-shot retry for nothing; a held run\\u0027s task instead stays \\u0060Claimed\\u0060, its worktree and lease intact, so the eventual relaunch resumes exactly where it left off. \\u0060LaunchHoldMonitor\\u0060\\u0027s own probe relaunches the single oldest held run on a doubling backoff (floor \\u0060SessionErrorRetryBackoff\\u0060, cap \\u0060LaunchHoldProbeBackoffMaxInterval\\u0060) rather than every held run at once, so a still-broken node is not hammered with a full backlog of relaunches on every tick. \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 names the cause text and the likely fix (a NEEDS YOU line for an authentication failure names signing back in) rather than showing the task queue as merely stalled; \\u0060h9k daemon status\\u0060 names the same cause alongside the hold\\u0027s start time and probe count, without the fix, since \\u0060h9k status\\u0060 already carries it. **What a fix session added on top of the original design, and why.** An independent pre-PR review (cycle 1, both lenses) found four ways the hold itself could wedge open or leak: \\u0060LaunchHoldEngine.HeldRunsAsync\\u0060 only matched \\u0060RunDetails.NodeId\\u0060, so a Now-speed auto-pr-review sentinel run \\u2014 dispatched under the ceiling-exempt \\u0060Guid.Empty\\u0060 \\u2014 was held but never found again by the probe, the same sentinel-widening \\u0060RunSupervisor\\u0060 and \\u0060TokenBudgetRetryEngine\\u0060 already carry for identical reasons; \\u0060RunSupervisor.ResumeLaunchHeldRunAsync\\u0060 left a run whose task claim had moved on (an abandon, a lease-expiry reclaim) sitting \\u0060LaunchHeld\\u0060 forever rather than retiring it, so it kept winning the oldest-held sort and starved every other held run\\u0027s own probe; \\u0060RunSupervisor.CompleteRunAsync\\u0060 and \\u0060ReviewEngine.ClearLaunchHoldIfEvidencedAsync\\u0060 cleared the hold on any non-zero-work result, including one from a session that had been running since before the hold was ever raised \\u2014 proof that session eventually finished, not that a fresh launch works now \\u2014 so \\u0060LaunchHoldEngine.ClearIfEvidencedAsync\\u0060 now also requires the completing session\\u0027s own process to have started at or after the hold\\u0027s raise before it counts as evidence; and the node stream\\u0027s own unversioned appends could lose a concurrent write under \\u0060EventStreamUnexpectedMaxEventIdException\\u0060 and escape into an unrelated catch, so \\u0060LaunchHoldEngine\\u0060 now retries its own load-decide-append-save cycle a bounded number of times rather than dropping the write, since every operation on that stream (a join, a probe, a clear) is commutative against fresh state, unlike the task-stream generation fence elsewhere in this daemon where the same exception means a stale write must be dropped. The same review also caught the auto-pr-review \\u0022now\\u0022 speed\\u0027s own claim-and-launch path bypassing the hold entirely, since it dispatches through \\u0060RunLauncher\\u0060 directly rather than through \\u0060DispatchEngine\\u0060\\u0027s claim gate \\u2014 \\u0060AutoPrReviewEngine\\u0060 now reads the hold fresh for each candidate, since a hold raised mid-sweep by an earlier candidate\\u0027s own failure must still be seen by the ones after it, and defers a Now-speed candidate to the ordinary queue-first slot while it stands, the same deferral an immediate-launch-cap candidate already takes. **Does this block the later vision?** No: the hold is per-node state on the existing node stream, gates one existing claim loop, and the probe is one more prompt prose moves out of C# string literals into markdown template files that \\u0060h9k install\\u0060 publishes beside the canonical skill set (\\u0060~/.hall9k/templates\\u0060, never inside \\u0060~/.hall9k/skills\\u0060), while every token a parser matches back out of an agent session\\u0027s output stays a literal in code, injected into the assembled prompt rather than typed into a template; this branch ships the mechanism and proves it end to end on one full builder, \\u0060ReviewLapPromptBuilder\\u0060.** Why: \\u0060AgentPromptBuilder.cs\\u0060 (4,311 lines), \\u0060WorkPromptBuilder.cs\\u0060 (2,125 lines) and \\u0060ReviewLapPromptBuilder.cs\\u0060 (764 lines) carry roughly 1,650 \\u0060AppendLine\\u0060 calls of judgment-layer wording \\u2014 the norms, the working rules, the explanations a session reads to decide how to behave \\u2014 with no way for an operator to read, diff, or override any of it short of rebuilding the daemon. Doctrine (added to \\u0060AGENTS.md\\u0060): Hall9k is prescriptive about the lifecycle and permissive about judgment; the template layer (this task) and the skill layer (already shipped) are the judgment side, while the parsed contracts stay fixed in code because an operator\\u0027s edit to one of those would silently break machine parsing rather than merely read differently to the agent. **Scope, ruled by Brian (2026-09-11), not a choice this branch made for itself:** this branch is slice one of the migration. \\u0060WorkPromptBuilder.cs\\u0060, \\u0060AgentPromptBuilder.cs\\u0060, and \\u0060ReviewEngine\\u0060\\u0027s own merged-reviewer preamble are follow-up tasks \\u0060e339ec23\\u0060 and \\u00606bb76ddf\\u0060, both blocked on this one landing first; neither file is touched here. The golden-file proof below is the reproducible evidence that carries the migration\\u0027s own no-behavior-change claim forward to those follow-ups: \\u0060UPDATE_GOLDENS=1\\u0060 run against \\u0060ReviewLapPromptBuilder\\u0060 on \\u0060main\\u0060 (its pre-migration, string-literal form) regenerates the same four fixtures byte-for-byte, so a follow-up run can check its own builder\\u0027s migration against the identical proof. \\u0060RESOLUTION:\\u0060 remaining a literal in three places (\\u0060ReviewResultParser\\u0060\\u0027s own inline check, \\u0060PrSummaryParser.ResolutionMarker\\u0060, and this task\\u0027s own \\u0060PromptContractTokens\\u0060 aggregator \\u2014 see the contract inventory below) is recorded here as a residual for whichever of \\u0060e339ec23\\u0060/\\u00606bb76ddf\\u0060 first moves prose beside a caller of \\u0060ReviewResultParser.ParseFixOutcome\\u0060, since that is the first point the duplication can be collapsed onto one shared constant.
